newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU reforms to top Dutch EU presidency agenda.
newsitem.headline: EU reforms to top Dutch EU presidency agenda.

text.p: The Netherlands said on Wednesday it would give top priority to reforming the European Union's institutions during its six-month presidency of the European Council from January 1.

Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo said in a "presidency" policy document, to be debated in the Dutch parliament on November 28, that he hoped work on the inter-governmental conference (IGC) on EU reform could be completed by the EU summit in Amsterdam next June.

"The Netherlands hopes that the inter-governmental conference in Amsterdam will result in the reform of the Union's institutions in the interests of greater effectiveness, openness and democracy," the document said.
"The will is present...but there can, of course, be no guarantee that this will in fact happen at the European Summit."

The Netherlands also wants to ensure progress on the run-up to Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) and the planned single currency, as well as seeking measures to combat international organised crime and drug trafficking.
"The illegal drug trade and international crime are regarded in the Union as the most critical threat of the moment," Van Mierlo said.
